C073.notes: SER NA-US-002. Dual-date 1776–1976 drummer-boy reverse (Jack L. Ahr). Clad sandwich on the edges — not 40% silver. Classic American “save the bicentennials” tube: twenty-six pieces someone pulled from change in the years after the party, thinking history might pay. It mostly pays in face and memory — Washington still on the front, a colonial drummer on the back, a whole summer of ’76 in a plastic cylinder. First USA circulating-lot flip (albums + Meijer token already on the board). Flip cards now 76. SER siblings: NA-US-001 · tokens NA-US-003…006.
C073.story: A 1976 25 cents from USA. The obverse shows Washington; the reverse shows drummer boy (Jack L. Ahr); dual-date 1776–1976, E PLURIBUS UNUM, QUARTER DOLLAR. Struck in Cu-Ni clad (copper core visible on reeded edges).

C088.notes: SER NA-US-001. Mid-Eisenhower pocket change — still real silver before the 1965 clad cut. Junk Ag = melt (see SILVER.md). Sister to the Roosevelt album run (A003–A005). Vault Ag ~51.938 → ~52.01 oz. SER siblings USA: NA-US-002…006. USA flips now 6 (incl. tokens).
C088.story: A 1957 10 ¢ Roosevelt from USA. The obverse shows Roosevelt left (John R. Sinnock); the reverse shows torch; olive, oak, UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, ONE DIME. Struck in 90% silver.

T003.notes: SER NA-US-005. FREE PONY RIDE // MEIJER IS FOR KIDS. Midwest grocery lore — Sandy’s been a penny ride since 1962 (Fred Meijer cut it from 10¢). Kids’ hands, cart handles, then a flip. Tokens now T001–T003. SER siblings: NA-US-003 · NA-US-004 · NA-US-006.

T004.notes: SER NA-US-006. Card reads NEW NIXON PENNY / AND GETTING SMALLER · miniature cent in the window · user: Want a fun one? Good luck valuation + photo. Early-70s inflation satire — Watergate-era pocket joke about the shrinking dollar under Nixon, sold as a gag souvenir, not a Mint product. Valuation is soft: common novelty, condition lives in the cardboard. Fun vault texture next to Meijer pony T003 / NA-US-005. Tokens now T001–T004.
